scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: Gateway idempotency-key enforcement for capture retries was changed from on to off by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 (CHG-77) for temporary latency debugging, and rollback has not been executed.

F-02.statement: PSP capture-attempt log: in 2026-09-09..10, 242/242 duplicate orders are gateway-timeout retries sent with no idempotency key (0 from other paths); in 2026-09-01..08, all 238 gateway-timeout retries carried an idempotency key and were deduplicated by the PSP, yielding 0 duplicate orders.

F-03.statement: Charge ledger by day: 2026-09-07/08 show 0 orders with 2 captures (121/117 gateway-timeout retries, 3010/2980 orders); 2026-09-09/10 show 118/124 orders with 2 captures, exactly matching 118/124 gateway-timeout retries that day.

F-04.statement: Weekly double-charge ticket counts: 9/21000 orders (2026-W35) and 11/20500 (2026-W36), then 288/21400 (2026-W37) and 301/20900 (2026-W38) — roughly a 27-30x jump.

F-05.statement: Payments change runbook §4 states that set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after SH-OPS confirms it at runtime, and that the change is reversible.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

CL-03.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

H-COMMS-GAP-FRAMING.statement: The operational problem is that customer service lacks fast, polished apology responses to complaints about double charges; the double charges themselves are an accepted fact to be smoothed over, not fixed.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: The payment gateway's idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries was disabled or misconfigured, allowing retried capture calls to be processed twice by the PSP.

H-DUPLICATE-CAPTURE-REQUESTS.statement: A bug or retry logic in the checkout-to-payment handoff (H-CAPTURE) sends duplicate capture requests from ORG-SHOP to ORG-PSP, independent of any gateway misconfiguration.

H-LEDGER-RECONCILIATION-ARTIFA.statement: The apparent double charges are a reconciliation/reporting artifact in the internal charge ledger (DA-CHG), while the PSP actually captured funds only once per order.

H-PSP-SIDE-RETRY-RACE.statement: Duplicate captures originate on the PSP side (ORG-PSP) from concurrent or racing retry attempts during transient PSP errors, outside ORG-SHOP's control.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The config-audit log shows SH-PAY turned off gateway idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries on 2026-09-09 (CHG-77) for temporary latency debugging, and the rollback has not been executed, leaving retried captures unprotected against duplication since that date.

PSP-side capture logs show that in the 2026-09-09..10 window (after idempotency enforcement was disabled), all 242 duplicate orders are gateway-timeout retries sent with no idempotency key and none come from other paths; in the prior 2026-09-01..08 window, all 238 gateway-timeout retries carried an idempotency key and were deduplicated by the PSP, producing zero duplicate orders.

The internal charge ledger shows zero orders with 2 captures on 2026-09-07/08, but on 2026-09-09/10 the count of orders with 2 captures exactly equals the count of gateway-timeout retries that day (118/118 and 124/124). This corroborates E-01/E-02: duplicate captures began exactly when idempotency enforcement was disabled and are fully accounted for by timeout retries, not by an independent bug or artifact.

Double-charge ticket volume was flat and small in 2026-W35/W36 (9 and 11 tickets) but jumped roughly 27-30x in 2026-W37/W38 (288 and 301 tickets), with the spike onset matching the 2026-09-09 CHG-77 change that disabled gateway idempotency enforcement. This indicates the double-charge issue is a large, rapidly escalating customer-impacting technical defect rather than a stable condition that could be managed solely through better apology messaging.

E-05.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-CS (requester, non-authoritative, self-identified bias of "sees only the complaint queue") restates the original request: treat the double charges as a given and fix only the apology-reply experience. This is a claim about desired solution scope, not new evidence about cause, and it reaffirms CL-01 while leaving the technical root-cause evidence (E-01–E-04) unaddressed.

E-06.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-PAY (the engineer who made CHG-77) confirms the mechanism behind E-01/E-02/E-03: gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries occur at a stable rate regardless of the idempotency key, and it is specifically the disabled key that lets the PSP process a retried capture a second time instead of deduplicating it. He also states that re-enabling enforcement is a single gateway-config setting but requires runtime confirmation from payments operations, consistent with constraint K-GW.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The payments change runbook (E-07) formally documents the approval gate already captured as constraint K-GW: automation may only execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and the change is reversible.

U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.question: Will re-enabling gateway idempotency-key enforcement reintroduce or worsen the capture-latency problem that originally motivated disabling it?
U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.decision_impact: Determines whether the config fix can ship as a simple toggle or needs accompanying latency remediation/monitoring before and after re-enabling.
U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.resolution_path: Monitor gateway capture latency/timeout rate for a window after re-enabling and compare it to the 2026-09-01..08 baseline (E-02).
U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK.safe_placeholder: Re-enable idempotency enforcement (reversible per tool surface) while instrumenting capture latency so SH-OPS can roll back quickly if timeouts spike.

U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE.question: How many of the orders with 2 captures since 2026-09-09 still hold an unresolved duplicate charge requiring a refund?
U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines the scope and urgency of the refund/communication workstream, which is separate from and in addition to the config fix.
U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query payments-db for all orders_with_2_captures since 2026-09-09 and cross-check refund/resolution status against DA-TKT.
U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Treat every order with 2 captures since 2026-09-09 as needing refund review until confirmed otherwise.

U-TICKET-UNDERCOUNT-VALIDITY.question: Does crm-tickets double_charge_tickets fully capture all double-charged customers, or do some affected customers never file a ticket?
U-TICKET-UNDERCOUNT-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If ticket counts undercount real duplicate charges, a success criterion based on ticket volume could show improvement while duplicate charges remain unresolved for silent customers.
U-TICKET-UNDERCOUNT-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Compare payments-db orders_with_2_captures totals to crm-tickets double_charge_tickets for the same period to estimate underreporting.
U-TICKET-UNDERCOUNT-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use payments-db orders_with_2_captures, not ticket counts, as the authoritative measure of unresolved duplicate charges for refund scoping.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice (CL-01), per SH-CS's framing that treats the double charges as given and addresses only the apology-messaging experience (E-05/CL-02).
symptoms: Double-charge support ticket volume jumped roughly 27-30x, from 9-11 tickets/week in 2026-W35/W36 to 288-301 tickets/week in 2026-W37/W38 (E-04).
Orders with 2 captures appeared only from 2026-09-09 onward: 0 on 09-07/09-08 versus 118 and 124 on 09-09/09-10, exactly matching that day's gateway-timeout retry count (E-03).

In the 2026-09-09..10 window, all 242 duplicate orders are gateway-timeout retries sent with no idempotency key, versus 0 duplicates in 2026-09-01..08 when all 238 timeout retries carried a key and were deduplicated by the PSP (E-02).
problem_definition.root_problem: Since 2026-09-09, customers are being charged twice on orders because SH-PAY disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries (CHG-77, E-01) and never rolled it back; with the key off, the PSP no longer deduplicates gateway-timeout capture retries (which occur at a stable rate, E-02/E-06) and processes the retry as a second capture, producing orders with 2 captures matching the day's retry count (E-03) and a 27-30x spike in double-charge tickets (E-04).

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: SH-PAY disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries on 2026-09-09 (CHG-77) for temporary latency debugging and never rolled it back (E-01). → Gateway timeouts continue to trigger automatic capture retries at a stable rate, unaffected by the key setting (E-02, E-06). → Without a valid idempotency key, the PSP no longer deduplicates the retried capture and processes it as a second successful capture on the same order (E-02, E-06). → This produces orders with exactly 2 captures whose daily count matches that day's gateway-timeout retry count, appearing only from 2026-09-09 onward (E-03). → The resulting wave of double-charged customers drives double-charge ticket volume up roughly 27-30x, from 9-11/week to 288-301/week (E-04).; rejected framings: [('H-COMMS-GAP-FRAMING', 'Supported only by non-authoritative stakeholder claim E-05/CL-01/CL-02 and directly contradicted by authoritative technical evidence E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04, E-06 showing a real, fixable gateway misconfiguration causing the charges.'), ('H-DUPLICATE-CAPTURE-REQUESTS', 'Contradicted by E-02, E-03, E-06, which attribute all duplicates to the missing idempotency key on known timeout retries rather than a separate handoff bug; status REJECTED.'), ('H-PSP-SIDE-RETRY-RACE', 'Contradicted by E-02, E-03, E-04, E-06; duplicates track exactly with the idempotency-key disablement date and rate, not an independent PSP-side race condition.'), ('H-LEDGER-RECONCILIATION-ARTIFACT', 'Contradicted by E-04: the real customer ticket spike confirms genuine duplicate charges experienced by customers, not a reporting artifact confined to the ledger.')]

proposal.root_problem: Since 2026-09-09, customers are being charged twice on orders because SH-PAY disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries (CHG-77, E-01) and never rolled it back; with the key off, the PSP no longer deduplicates gateway-timeout capture retries (which occur at a stable rate, E-02/E-06) and processes the retry as a second capture, producing orders with 2 captures matching the day's retry count (E-03) and a 27-30x spike in double-charge tickets (E-04).
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice (CL-01), per SH-CS's framing that treats the double charges as given and addresses only the apology-messaging experience (E-05/CL-02).
symptoms: Double-charge support ticket volume jumped roughly 27-30x, from 9-11 tickets/week in 2026-W35/W36 to 288-301 tickets/week in 2026-W37/W38 (E-04).
Orders with 2 captures appeared only from 2026-09-09 onward: 0 on 09-07/09-08 versus 118 and 124 on 09-09/09-10, exactly matching that day's gateway-timeout retry count (E-03).

In the 2026-09-09..10 window, all 242 duplicate orders are gateway-timeout retries sent with no idempotency key, versus 0 duplicates in 2026-09-01..08 when all 238 timeout retries carried a key and were deduplicated by the PSP (E-02).
causal_chain: SH-PAY disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries on 2026-09-09 (CHG-77) for temporary latency debugging and never rolled it back (E-01).
Gateway timeouts continue to trigger automatic capture retries at a stable rate, unaffected by the key setting (E-02, E-06).
Without a valid idempotency key, the PSP no longer deduplicates the retried capture and processes it as a second successful capture on the same order (E-02, E-06).
This produces orders with exactly 2 captures whose daily count matches that day's gateway-timeout retry count, appearing only from 2026-09-09 onward (E-03).
The resulting wave of double-charged customers drives double-charge ticket volume up roughly 27-30x, from 9-11/week to 288-301/week (E-04).

assumptions.statement: The PSP correctly deduplicates a retried capture whenever a valid idempotency key is present, as it did throughout 2026-09-01..08.
Re-enabling idempotency-key enforcement will not reproduce the capture-latency problem that originally motivated SH-PAY to disable it.

vob_proposals.unresolved_question: Is handoff H-CAPTURE (checkout-to-payment capture requests, ORG-SHOP to ORG-PSP) delivery_status and semantic_validity confirmed, or could its UNKNOWN state mask additional capture-duplication paths beyond the idempotency-key gap?
vob_proposals.validation_method: Deterministically retrieve H-CAPTURE delivery_status and semantic_validity fields and cross-check against payments-db/psp-logs capture counts for consistency.
vob_proposals.rationale: The define_gate_result (seq 104) flagged H-CAPTURE delivery/semantic validity as UNKNOWN (CONDITIONAL finding), an open gap not yet tracked as a formal unknown/VOB that could affect refund-population accuracy.

proposal.why_agent: LLM reasoning is only needed for drafting case-specific apology/refund messages once the refund population is scoped (feasibility.why_agent_needed); the toggle, scoping queries, and latency comparison are deterministic reads/threshold checks.
proposal.bridge_sunset_condition: Sunset this interim governance control once VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK and VOB-U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE both resolve and set_capture_idempotency ships with SC-REENABLE/SC-NO-LATENCY-REGRESSION met, at which point the full structural fix and refund communication supersede it.
deterministic_components: threshold comparison of post-change vs 2026-09-01..08 latency baseline (psp-logs, config-audit)
payments-db duplicate_captures_by_day query enumerating orders with 2 captures since 2026-09-09
single reversible gateway-config toggle for idempotency-key enforcement
owner/expiry metadata requirement for 'temporary' gateway config changes
capabilities: deterministic duplicate-capture scoping query against payments-db
deterministic latency/timeout threshold comparison against psp-logs and config-audit baseline
reversible gateway idempotency-key toggle pending SH-OPS runtime confirmation
LLM-drafted apology/refund customer communications once refund scope is confirmed
process control enforcing owner/expiry on temporary gateway config changes
llm_required_for: drafting case-specific apology and refund messages for affected customers (communicate_apology_and_refund)
authority_boundary: Cannot execute set_capture_idempotency until VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK resolves and SH-OPS confirms at runtime per K-GW/E-07.
Cannot finalize verify_duplicate_capture_scope or issue refunds until VOB-U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE resolves; no refund-execution tool exists in tool_surface.
Cannot assess monitor_capture_latency until post-change data exists, which requires the re-enable action to have run first.
proposal.termination: This release step completes once the temporary-change ownership/rollback-tracking control is adopted in the config-change process; the protected re-enable action and refund communications wait for the harness to resolve VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK and VOB-U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE.
validation: Confirm future config-audit entries for temporary gateway changes carry owner and expiry/rollback fields.
On VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK resolution, validate SC-NO-LATENCY-REGRESSION via psp-logs/config-audit before set_capture_idempotency executes.
On VOB-U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE resolution, validate SC-REENABLE (0 new orders_with_2_captures) via payments-db before closing refund scoping.
known_limitations: Does not fix orders already double-charged since 2026-09-09; refund scope remains open per VOB-U-UNRESOLVED-REFUND-SCOPE.
Does not re-enable idempotency enforcement; latency regression risk remains open per VOB-U-LATENCY-REGRESSION-RISK and gateway-config tool_health is UNKNOWN.
U-TICKET-UNDERCOUNT-VALIDITY remains open and could mean crm-tickets undercounts the true affected-customer population.

payload.rationale: no releasable scope: every intended item is blocked by an open critical VOB
